original_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let k[x1, ..., xn] be the polynomial algebra, and let P and Q be locally nilpotent derivations of k[x1, ..., xn]. Consider the two one-parameter subgroups {exp(tP) | t in k} and {exp(tQ) | t in k} of Aut_k(k[x1, ..., xn]). Under what conditions is the minimal closed subgroup of Aut_k(k[x1, ..., xn]) that contains both of these one-parameter subgroups finite-dimensional?
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core content of Popov’s Problem 3.1: the base field is algebraically closed of characteristic 0, the ambient algebra is the polynomial ring in n variables, P and Q are locally nilpotent derivations, one considers their exponential one-parameter subgroups, and the question is exactly whether the smallest closed subgroup containing those subgroups is finite-dimensional.
missing_details: In the paper the ambient group is not the full automorphism group Aut_k(k[x_1,...,x_n]) but its closed normal subgroup G = Aut_k^*(k[x_1,...,x_n]), the special affine Cremona group of automorphisms with Jacobian determinant 1.
P and Q should be specified as k-derivations of A = k[x_1,...,x_n].
The sets {exp(tP) | t in k} and {exp(tQ) | t in k} are being viewed as one-dimensional unipotent algebraic subgroups of G.
The phrase "minimal closed subgroup" is meant relative to the infinite-dimensional algebraic group G; correspondingly, "finite-dimensional" means a finite-dimensional algebraic subgroup.
The paper imposes no extra hypotheses on P and Q: they are not assumed to commute, be homogeneous, satisfy degree bounds, or meet any rank condition.
The quantifier on n is arbitrary: the problem is posed for the polynomial algebra in n variables, with no restriction to a specific n.
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let A = k[x_1, ..., x_n], and let G = Aut_k^*(A) be the special affine Cremona group, i.e. the subgroup of k-automorphisms of A with Jacobian determinant 1. For locally nilpotent k-derivations P, Q of A, consider the one-dimensional unipotent subgroups U_P = {exp(tP) | t in k} and U_Q = {exp(tQ) | t in k} of G. When is the minimal closed subgroup of G containing U_P and U_Q a finite-dimensional algebraic subgroup?
justification: The draft is very close to the paper’s actual intent, but Popov formulates the question inside the special affine Cremona group fixed in Section 1, not merely inside the full automorphism group. Section 1 sets the notation A = k[x_1,...,x_n] over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, introduces G = Aut_k^*(A), and notes that exp(tD) lies in G for every locally nilpotent derivation D. Section 3 then states exactly the finiteness question for the minimal closed subgroup containing the two one-dimensional subgroups attached to P and Q. No additional assumptions such as commutativity or homogeneity appear in the problem as stated.

citations.label: introductory observation that exp(tD) lies in Aut_k^*(A) for locally nilpotent D
